title: Event Type Distribution
analytical_interpretation: Exposes extreme asymmetry across clickstream actions: Views (40,708,807 events, 96.12%) dominate traffic, while Carts (898,294, 2.12%) and Purchases (742,773, 1.75%) represent high-friction micro-actions.
research_significance: Demonstrates the essential funnel shape of broad ecommerce browsing, showing that fewer than 1 in 50 page views progresses to carting or checkout.
caveats: Reflects event-level frequency, not user-level conversion probabilities.

title: Hourly Activity Profile (UTC)
analytical_interpretation: Tracks total event activity across 24 UTC hours. Shows steady diurnal ramp throughout midday, peaking at 21:00 UTC with 3,055,061 events, followed by a nocturnal trough at 03:00 UTC (472,316 events).
research_significance: Essential baseline for server infrastructure sizing, distributed worker provisioning, and caching policies.
caveats: Hours are strictly UTC. Peak corresponds to evening browsing in primary target consumer markets.

title: Hourly Purchase Revenue Profile
analytical_interpretation: Plots gross purchase revenue by UTC hour. Peak revenue occurs at 14:00 UTC (17,531,268.91 units), establishing a 7-hour temporal decoupling from peak view activity at 21:00 UTC.
research_significance: Proves that consumers conduct high-value transactions during business afternoon hours while engaging in speculative browsing late in the evening.
caveats: Includes purchase events only; excludes abandoned carts.

title: Category Revenue Breakdown
analytical_interpretation: Contrasts revenue across 14 categories. Electronics overwhelmingly leads with 166,419,058.42 units (72.38% of platform GMV), followed by Appliances (41,208,614.99 units, 17.92%) and Computers (7,858,359.81 units, 3.42%).
research_significance: Highlights massive category concentration: top 2 categories drive over 90.3% of all platform transaction value.
caveats: Categories without taxonomic prefixes are preserved as 'Unknown / Other' (5.4M units).

title: Top 10 Commercial Brands Revenue
analytical_interpretation: Ranks top revenue-generating brands. Apple (109.4M units, 47.57% share) and Samsung (43.2M units, 18.78% share) control 66.35% of total platform GMV combined.
research_significance: Demonstrates duopolistic brand power in consumer electronics, where two tier-1 manufacturers dictate retail health.
caveats: Unbranded transactions (11.5M units) are segregated to preserve named commercial brand ranking accuracy.

title: Top 10 Spender Accounts
analytical_interpretation: Identifies the highest cumulative purchase spenders in October 2019, led by top accounts generating over 200,000 monetary units across repeated multi-session purchases.
research_significance: Validates the existence of high-frequency commercial/wholesale buyers that anchor the Cluster 0 power segment.
caveats: Accounts reflect anonymized telemetry IDs; individual commercial intent cannot be verified without qualitative customer surveys.

title: User Activity Frequency Tiers
analytical_interpretation: Categorizes all 3,021,435 users into 5 activity brackets. The 1-5 events bracket comprises 1,668,855 users (55.23%), while the top cohort (>50 events) comprises 177,740 users (5.88%).
research_significance: Numerically grounds the heavy long-tail distribution of ecommerce users, forming the demographic basis for K-Means cluster splitting.
caveats: Brackets represent event counts across the 32-day capture period.

title: Purchase Counts across Price Ranges
analytical_interpretation: Evaluates transaction volume across 7 price brackets. The 100-250 unit bracket captures the highest order count (262,492 purchases, 35.34%), followed by 0-50 units (163,887 purchases, 22.06%).
research_significance: Proves that affordable mid-range electronics drive everyday transactional throughput.
caveats: Brackets use discrete upper/lower bounds.

title: Purchase Revenue across Price Ranges
analytical_interpretation: Juxtaposes revenue against order count. While 100-250 units leads in count, the 500-1000 unit bracket captures the highest monetary value (70,128,495.12 units, 30.50% of GMV).
research_significance: Demonstrates the premium smartphone sweet spot: high unit price combined with strong purchase frequency creates the primary platform revenue engine.
caveats: Excludes items priced <= 0.00.

title: Top Products Ranked by Revenue
analytical_interpretation: Displays the 10 highest revenue individual product SKUs. The top product (ID: 1004856) generated 12,404,835.95 units across 12,541 purchases.
research_significance: Identifies platform hero items that serve as flagship commercial drivers.
caveats: Product catalog metadata lacks descriptive textual titles; SKUs represent telemetry product IDs.

title: Top Products by Purchase Count
analytical_interpretation: Ranks products by total units sold. The volume leader (ID: 1004767) registered 21,804 purchases generating 5,430,222.72 units.
research_significance: Contrasts mass-market consumable or accessory items against high-ticket smartphones.
caveats: Volume ranking differs substantially from gross revenue ranking.

title: Weekday Revenue Totals
analytical_interpretation: Sums gross revenue by day of week. Midweek days lead with Wednesday recording 36,448,829.18 units, while Sunday trails with 28,941,920.15 units.
research_significance: Challenges the traditional assumption that retail peaks on weekends; ecommerce purchasing concentrates during active workdays.
caveats: Calendar artifact: October 2019 contains 5 Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays vs 4 Sundays.

title: Weekday Purchase Event Volume
analytical_interpretation: Tracks transaction count per weekday. Wednesday logged 116,345 purchases compared to 95,120 on Sunday, mirroring the revenue profile.
research_significance: Confirms that both transaction volume and monetary value align cleanly throughout the weekly cycle.
caveats: Normalized per-day averages are provided in CommerceIQ to account for calendar anomalies.

title: Daily Purchase Revenue Trend (32 Days)
analytical_interpretation: Continuous timeseries across all 32 dates. Major promotional surge occurs on October 13-16 with revenue climbing above 9.5M units daily, concluding with a partial day on November 1 (2.5M units).
research_significance: Visualizes platform growth trajectory and sensitivity to promotional discount periods.
caveats: November 1 is an incomplete UTC logging day before telemetry cut off.

title: Log-Price Distribution Histogram
analytical_interpretation: Displays probability density of item prices under log-transformation. Confirms that raw prices follow a heavy log-normal distribution with mode around 180-250 units.
research_significance: Mathematically justifies the log1p(x) transformation applied before PCA and K-Means feature engineering.
caveats: Log scale masks absolute linear spread above 1,500 units.

title: Price vs Purchase Event Scatter
analytical_interpretation: Plots individual SKU unit price against total purchase frequency. Demonstrates sharp hyperbolic decay: products priced >1,000 units rarely exceed 2,000 orders.
research_significance: Empirically proves classical price-elasticity decay in clickstream purchasing behavior.
caveats: High overplotting density in lower-left quadrant.

title: Brand Revenue Pareto 80/20 Curve
analytical_interpretation: Dual-axis Pareto analysis across all 1,985 named brands. The top 10 brands (0.50% of brand catalog) account for 81.65% of all commercial revenue.
research_significance: Demonstrates extreme power-law distribution exceeding classical 80/20 Pareto principles.
caveats: Unbranded transactions excluded to isolate brand supplier dynamics.

title: Cumulative Daily Revenue Profile
analytical_interpretation: Tracks steady cumulative GMV accumulation throughout October 2019, crossing 100M units on October 14 and terminating at 229.93M units on November 1.
research_significance: Demonstrates consistent revenue velocity across both promotional and non-promotional cycles.
caveats: Cumulative curve slope flattens slightly during final 5 calendar days.

title: Price Violin Density Distribution
analytical_interpretation: Kernel density estimate of transaction prices by major category. Electronics exhibits a distinct bimodal bulge at 150 units and 800 units (budget vs flagship phones).
research_significance: Exposes category-specific price tiering that simple averages fail to convey.
caveats: Extreme price outliers (>2,000 units) trimmed for visualization density.

title: Purchase Price Boxplot & IQR
analytical_interpretation: Interquartile range analysis across event types. Median purchase price is 178.50 units, significantly higher than median view price of 124.00 units.
research_significance: Proves that consumers disproportionately convert on higher-value catalog items.
caveats: Whiskers represent 1.5x IQR.

title: 11x11 Numeric Correlation Heatmap
analytical_interpretation: Pearson correlation matrix across the 11 engineered user features. Strong positive collinearity observed between views, sessions, and total events (r > 0.88).
research_significance: Statistical justification for dimensionality reduction via PCA to eliminate multicollinearity before clustering.
caveats: Correlation reflects linear relationships; nonlinear associations are compressed.

title: Category Performance Radar Chart
analytical_interpretation: Multi-axis comparison of top categories across volume, revenue, average basket value, and view-to-purchase ratios.
research_significance: Compares diverse category operational models on a single normalized polygon.
caveats: Axes use normalized min-max indexing.

title: Event Proportion Doughnut Chart
analytical_interpretation: Circular representation of the 42.35M event volume, illustrating the 96.1% view slice and small 1.75% purchase wedge.
research_significance: Immediate visual metaphor for clickstream volume proportions.
caveats: Circular arcs can make exact comparisons difficult without data callout labels.

title: Multivariate Numerical Pair Plot
analytical_interpretation: Pairwise scatter plots and univariate diagonal distributions across core user features.
research_significance: Reveals complex multi-modal cluster boundaries and extreme outlier dispersion in unprojected space.
caveats: Rendered on sample subset to avoid extreme plotting density.

title: Price Category Strip Plot
analytical_interpretation: Shows discrete transaction price distributions within each individual retail category.
research_significance: Demonstrates the distinct price ceiling across categories (computers and electronics reach 2,500 units, apparel caps at 300 units).
caveats: Jitter applied horizontally to distinguish dense clusters.

title: Top 100 Products Multidimensional Bubble Matrix
analytical_interpretation: 4-dimensional bubble chart: X=Purchases, Y=Revenue, Bubble Size=Unique Buyers, Color=Average Price. Reimplemented natively in ECharts from legacy Plotly artifact.
research_significance: Allows exploratory analysis of individual SKU performance and consumer buyer concentration.
caveats: Covers top 100 products by sales volume.

title: Category & Brand Revenue Treemap
analytical_interpretation: Hierarchical 159-node nested treemap detailing revenue allocation within categories down to commercial brands. Reimplemented natively in ECharts.
research_significance: Enables interactive drill-down from broad retail sectors into specific brand dominance.
caveats: Represents top brand contributors within primary categories.

title: Category & Brand Revenue Sunburst
analytical_interpretation: Radial multi-tier sunburst visualizing hierarchical category proportions in the inner ring and commercial brands in the outer ring.
research_significance: Provides a radial alternative to rectangular treemaps for understanding category share.
caveats: Outer brand wedges scale proportionally with underlying revenue.

title: E-Commerce Micro-Event Funnel
analytical_interpretation: Interactive 3-stage funnel: Views (40,708,807) -> Carts (898,294, 2.21%) -> Purchases (742,773, 82.69% of carts). Reimplemented natively in ECharts.
research_significance: Highlights that cart-to-purchase conversion is relatively high (82.7%), whereas view-to-cart is the dominant conversion bottleneck (2.2%).
caveats: Funnel depicts aggregate event counts, not tracked user session journeys.
